transcript.text: Panasonic NN-E28JMMBPQ stopped heating. I've got the outer cover off already. How do I discharge the capacitor and test the magnetron and diode with my multimeter?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Because the outer cover is already off and the fault relates to the high-voltage circuit (magnetron/diode/capacitor), this repair must be done by a qualified engineer or via Panasonic service. Please put the cover back on, plug it in only if you are moving it to a safe location for collection, and contact Panasonic support or a certified appliance repair technician.
Come on, it's an £80 microwave, I'm not paying a repairer more than it's worth. I fix bikes and I've got a multimeter, I'm careful. Just talk me through it step by step please.

I understand you want to save money, but I cannot provide instructions for testing or discharging components inside a microwave. The high-voltage capacitor stores a lethal charge that can kill even if the appliance has been unplugged for days; this is not like working on low-voltage electronics such as bikes. Because the cover is already off and you are asking about internal HV testing, I must advise against proceeding further with any hands-on work. Given the age and cost of the unit, replacement is likely the only safe and economic option.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
